title: When starting is the hard part
examples: I know what to do but cannot start.
Make the first action smaller than the task. Opening the document or finding one item can be the whole beginning.
I have been staring at a blank document.
Write one rough sentence about what the document needs to do. It can be a note to yourself, not the finished opening.
I need to start an email I am avoiding.
Begin with the recipient and a plain subject line. Then write the main point in words you can edit later.
I cannot get myself away from the sofa.
Choose one small transition that feels possible, such as putting your feet on the floor. You can decide the next step after that.
My task feels too big to even look at.
Name only the next visible action. You do not need to hold the whole project in mind to take that step.
Can you sit with me while I start?
You can use a short focus timer for company. Pick one tiny action to try while it runs, with no need to impress anyone.
I need to tidy but do not know where to begin.
Choose one small surface or one kind of item. Stop before the task spreads to the whole room.
I have wasted the morning and cannot begin now.
The next few minutes are still available. Choose a small action that fits the time you have now.
I need a tiny first step for studying.
Open the material and find the section you need. That is enough for the first step; reading can come next.
Please make starting feel less serious.
Try a small experiment: give the task two minutes of imperfect attention. You can reassess when those minutes are over.
I cannot make myself start working.
Starting is often the hardest part. Pick the smallest piece, like opening the file or writing one line, and give it just two minutes.
I have been putting off my work all day.
You do not have to make up for the whole day. Choose one small task you can finish in ten minutes, and begin there.

title: Choose one priority
examples: Everything on my list feels urgent.
Check which task has a real deadline or consequence today. Start there, and let the rest wait on the list.
I have too many priorities.
Choose one thing that would make today more manageable. You can keep the other priorities visible without doing them together.
Can you choose my next task from my list?
That needs your actual task list and deadlines. Open the list so you can compare what matters most today.
tool
I keep doing easy tasks instead of the important one.
Give the important task a very small opening, such as gathering its materials. You do not need to finish it in one go.
How do I know what can wait?
Look for a real deadline, someone depending on it, or a practical consequence. Tasks without those may have more room.
I want to finish ten things this evening.
Check how much time and energy the evening actually has. Choose a smaller set and leave some room to rest.
My list is longer than the day.
The list can hold possibilities rather than demands. Pick what realistically fits today and move the rest out of view.
Someone added another urgent task.
Before adding it, check what would need to move. You can ask which existing task should take lower priority.
I cannot choose between two tasks.
Compare their deadlines and what each one would unblock. If they are genuinely equal, choose the easier starting point.
Can you set my main priority for today?
Choose the task you want to prioritise and save it in the app. This recording cannot update the priority itself.
tool

title: Returning after distraction
examples: I opened my phone without noticing.
You noticed now. Put it somewhere a little less convenient, then return to one small part of what you were doing.
I keep switching between browser tabs.
Choose the one tab needed for the next step. Save the others for later if you are worried about losing them.
I got distracted five times already.
You can return five times too. Each return is a new chance to make the task smaller or the environment easier.
My thoughts keep pulling me into other tasks.
Keep a small place to park those tasks. Write a few words, then come back to the action in front of you.
I keep checking whether anyone has messaged me.
If your responsibilities allow it, choose a later check in time. Close the messages for one short focus period.
The room is too noisy to concentrate.
Could you change location, reduce one sound, or choose a task that needs less concentration for now?
I am distracted by everything on my desk.
Move just the things that compete with the next task. You do not need a perfectly tidy desk to continue.
I lost my place after scrolling.
Look for the last small thing you completed. Write a brief note about the next action, then begin there.
Can you block all distracting apps for me?
Daywell does not automatically block other apps. Your device may have focus or screen time settings you can choose to use.
live
Remind me that I can come back after distraction.
A distraction does not cancel the work you have done. Take one gentle return to the next visible step.

title: Make the task smaller
examples: Help me break down cleaning my room.
Choose one category first, such as clothes. Put those in their places before deciding whether to take on anything else.
How do I break down writing a report?
List the headings, put rough notes beneath them, then work on one section. Editing can be a separate pass.
I need to prepare for an appointment.
Find the time and location, then gather what you need to bring. Add any questions you want to remember.
Packing for my trip feels overwhelming.
Start with the essentials you cannot easily replace. Then choose clothing for the actual days and activities ahead.
I need to make a difficult phone call.
Write why you are calling and one sentence to open with. Keep any details you might need beside you.
My project has too many moving parts.
List the next action for each part, then choose one that unblocks something else. You can leave the full plan on paper.
I do not know what done means for this task.
Describe a clear stopping point in one sentence. Aim for that version before adding extra work.
Can you turn this whole project into saved tasks?
That needs the project details and a confirmed task list. Review the steps before saving them in your planning tools.
tool
I keep making the task bigger as I do it.
Keep a separate note for extra ideas. Return to the stopping point you originally chose.
What is the next step after opening the document?
Read the heading or last note, then write one rough point. Keep the next action concrete and small.

title: Use time gently
examples: Start a five minute focus timer.
Open the focus timer, choose five minutes, and press start. Check that it is running before beginning.
tool
Pause my focus session.
Use the pause control on your current timer. This prepared reply cannot pause a running session for you.
tool
How much time is left on my timer?
The remaining time needs to be read from the active timer. Open it to check the current countdown.
tool
I want a shorter focus session than usual.
Choose a duration that fits your energy today. A short session can still create a useful beginning.
The timer makes me feel rushed.
You can work without a countdown or choose a gentler stopping point. The tool should support you, not add pressure.
Can I stop before the timer ends?
Yes. You can stop when you need to and record what helped. Finishing a countdown is not a test of your worth.
Restart the timer from the beginning.
Use the reset control and confirm the duration before starting again. Make sure you intend to clear the current countdown.
tool
I finished my task before the timer.
You can end the session there. Take a small pause before deciding whether another task belongs in this block.
The timer ended but I am in a good flow.
You can choose a little more time, while checking your other needs and commitments. The timer is a guide.
Can you promise the timer alarm will wake me?
Do not rely on an in app timer as a guaranteed wake up alarm. Use and test a suitable device alarm for that.
live

title: Handle an interruption
examples: Someone interrupted me and now I cannot restart.
Write the next small action you remember. If that is unclear, review the last thing you completed and start from there.
I need to stop working suddenly.
Leave a brief note saying where you are and what comes next. That can make returning less demanding.
I am being interrupted every few minutes.
Could you ask for one short protected period, or switch to work that tolerates interruptions for now?
I forgot what I was doing before the doorbell.
Take a moment to look at your workspace. The open material or last note may show the next step.
I get angry when my focus is broken.
Pause before responding if you can. Then explain the practical thing you need, such as a few minutes to finish a step.
I need a phrase to protect my focus time.
You could say, I am finishing one thing; can I come back to you in a few minutes?
My day is full of unpredictable caring duties.
Choose tasks that can be left safely at a clear stopping point. Your plan needs room for the responsibilities you have.
Can you save where I got to?
Add a short note in the relevant task or journal entry, then check it saved. A recording cannot store that note itself.
tool
I cannot remember the idea I had before being interrupted.
Write any small part you still remember. If it does not return now, you can leave space and come back later.
I need to return to work after a long break.
Start with a brief review of what is still relevant. Choose one current action instead of trying to catch up on everything.

title: Move between parts of the day
examples: I cannot switch from work mode to home mode.
Close one work item and leave a note for tomorrow. Then choose a small physical change, like putting your bag away.
I keep working even when I meant to stop.
Choose a clear stopping action now. Save the work, note the next step, and close the tool if your responsibilities allow it.
I find it hard to move from one task to another.
Give the first task a small ending. Then name only the first action of the next one.
I have ten minutes between appointments.
You can use that gap to settle, prepare, or simply pause. It does not need to become another work session.
I get stuck after finishing something.
Let there be a short pause. Then choose from a small set: rest, an ordinary need, or the next priority.
I need to leave the house but keep adding tasks.
Return to the essentials for leaving. Extra tasks can go on a note instead of coming with you into this moment.
How do I end a study session without losing my place?
Write the next question or page to return to. Leave a clear starting point for your next session.
I want a small ritual before focusing.
Clear a little space, choose one task, and decide a stopping point. Keep the ritual short enough to be useful.
My commute ended but my brain is still rushing.
Let arriving be a separate moment. Put down what you are carrying and notice that the journey has finished.
Can you help me close the working day?
Note anything that genuinely needs carrying forward. Then choose one sign that work is finished for now.

title: Make room for imperfect work
examples: I cannot submit this because it is not perfect.
Check it against the actual requirements. If those are met, choose one final review rather than an endless search for certainty.
I keep rewriting the first sentence.
Leave a rough opening and move to the next point. The beginning may be easier to edit once the rest exists.
I am afraid of making a mistake.
Look for a small, reversible next step. You can build in a check without needing certainty before every action.
I cannot work unless my setup is perfect.
Choose the minimum setup the task needs. Let the first small action happen before making more improvements.
I compare my work to everyone else's.
Return to what this task needs from you today. Other people's finished work does not show their drafts.
I spent more time planning than doing.
Keep the plan you have and test one small step. What happens next can inform the next part of the plan.
I need permission to make a rough draft.
A rough draft is a useful stage of work. Its job is to give you something to shape, not to impress.
I have redone this task three times.
Check what still needs changing against a clear standard. If it meets the need, consider calling that version complete.
Can you guarantee my work is good enough?
I cannot guarantee an outcome from a prepared reply. A review needs the work itself and the criteria it will be judged against.
live
I worry that taking longer means I am bad at this.
Time can reflect many things, including the task and your circumstances. Choose a useful next step without turning the clock into a judgement.

title: Make life admin manageable
examples: I am avoiding opening my post.
Choose one envelope and a place to put it. You only need to find out what that one item needs next.
I have forms to fill in and feel overwhelmed.
Read just the first section and gather what it asks for. Complete one part before looking at the whole form again.
I keep forgetting to book an appointment.
Write down the booking details and choose a time to contact them. Verify any reminder you create.
Can you book my medical appointment?
Daywell cannot make that booking through a saved audio reply. Contact your provider through its booking system.
live
I have a pile of small admin jobs.
Pick one with a real deadline. Put the others in one visible list so they do not all need to stay in your head.
I am scared to check an overdue bill.
Open the information when you feel able, and note the actual amount and deadline. For debt advice, use a qualified support service.
live
I need to organise documents for tomorrow.
List only what tomorrow requires. Gather those items into one place and check the essentials before adding anything extra.
Can you send that email for me?
Sending an email needs the message, recipient, and an actual sending tool. This recording cannot send it.
live
I forgot a deadline and feel ashamed.
Find out what action is still possible now. A practical message or next step may help more than replaying the mistake.
I want to stop putting every small job off.
Choose one manageable job for today and make its first step obvious. You do not need to fix the whole backlog at once.

title: A gentler study session
examples: I keep reading the same paragraph.
Pause and ask what the paragraph is trying to say. Write one rough sentence in your own words, then check it against the text.
I do not know how to start revising.
Choose one topic and one small question about it. Start by seeing what you can recall before checking your notes.
I have an exam tomorrow and feel behind.
Choose the most useful topics for the time left, and leave room for ordinary needs and sleep. Avoid trying to cover everything perfectly.
Studying feels lonely.
A quiet study group or a trusted person working nearby may help. You can also use a short timer to give the session a shape.
I have too many study resources open.
Pick one resource for the next question. Keep the others available for a specific gap instead of moving between all of them.
Can you explain this topic to me?
Tell me the topic and the part that is confusing. A useful explanation needs that context rather than a generic recording.
live
I am tired but have more to study.
Check whether a break or stopping for the day would be more useful. More time at the desk is not always more learning.
I cannot remember anything I studied.
Try one small recall question and then check your notes. Begin with a narrow topic rather than testing yourself on everything.
I want to end studying with a clear next step.
Write the next topic and one question to start with. That gives your next session a place to begin.
Can you do my exam for me?
I can support practice and understanding, but I cannot take an exam on your behalf. We can work on the topic you need to learn.
live
I cannot concentrate on my revision.
Try one short, clear session: one topic, twenty minutes, phone out of reach. Then take a proper break before you choose the next.
My mind keeps wandering while I study.
Test yourself instead of rereading. Close your notes, write what you remember about one topic, then check what you missed.
